cards.explanation: The answer is that the priest pronounces the person unclean. He sees two things at once: the hair in the spot has turned white, and the sore appears deeper than the skin. Verse 3 says, “…it is a skin disease. After the priest examines him, he must pronounce him unclean.” I don't pull a batch out of the oven on a hunch either. I look first, and so does the priest.

The answer is seven. Verse 4 says the priest “…shall isolate the infected person for seven days.” That's the in-between answer for a spot that isn't clearly a disease yet. It's a week of letting the spot show what it really is.

The answer is False. The person is not clean yet. Verse 5 says that if the infection is unchanged and hasn't spread, “…the priest must isolate him for another seven days.” A second week, then the priest examines again (Leviticus 13:6). The ruling comes after that.

The answer is clean. Verse 6 says that if the sore has faded and hasn't spread, “…the priest shall pronounce him clean; it is a rash.” The person must also wash his clothes and be clean. That's where the two weeks of waiting end.
The answer is clothes. Verse 6 says, “The person must wash his clothes and be clean.” It's a laundry day with good news attached, friends. I'd gladly do that wash.

The answer is a skin disease. Verse 8 says, “…the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a skin disease.” The spread is what changes the answer, because the rash was clean after the first two weeks only while it stayed put. Once it moves, the verdict moves with it.

The answer is True. Verse 11 says, “…it is a chronic skin disease and the priest must pronounce him unclean.” Then it adds, “He need not isolate him, for he is unclean.” No maybe week here. When the signs are this plain, the priest says so right away.

The answer is that the person is clean. This one makes everybody do a double take, me too. Verse 13 says, “Since it has all turned white, he is clean.” The disease covering the whole body, all turned white, is what makes the priest pronounce clean. Then verse 14 adds that raw flesh makes someone unclean.

The answer is that the person is clean. Verse 17 says, “…if the infection has turned white, the priest is to pronounce the infected person clean; then he is clean.” The raw flesh was unclean (Leviticus 13:15), but once it turns white, the answer changes.

The answer is white hair and beneath the skin. Verse 20 says, “…if it appears to be beneath the skin and the hair in it has turned white, the priest shall pronounce him unclean…” Those two signs together are what the priest is looking for.

The answer is scar. Verse 23 says, “…it is only the scar from the boil, and the priest shall pronounce him clean.” A spot that stays the same and doesn't spread is only left over from the boil. It's a reminder, not a problem.

The answer is yellow and thin. Verse 30 says, “…if it appears to be deeper than the skin and the hair in it is yellow and thin, the priest must pronounce him unclean…” The text calls it “…a scaly outbreak…” Every spot has its own sign, and this one is hair that's yellow and thin.

The answer is to shave except for the scaly area. Verse 33 says, “…the person must shave himself except for the scaly area.” Then the priest isolates him for another seven days. On the seventh day, the priest examines the scaly outbreak again (Leviticus 13:34).

The answer is False. Verse 36 says that if the scaly outbreak has spread, “…the priest need not look for yellow hair; the person is unclean.” Once the outbreak spreads, there's no need to go looking for yellow hair. Spreading settles it.

The answer is that it has healed. Verse 37 says that if the scaly outbreak is unchanged and black hair has grown in it, “…then it has healed. He is clean…” Black hair growing in it is the good sign here.

The answer is harmless, and it's good news. Verse 39 says, “…if the spots are dull white, it is a harmless rash that has broken out on the skin; the person is clean.” The priest looks, the spots are dull white, and the person is clean. I do a happy dance right here on my gold base. Dull white spots, harmless rash, clean.

The answer is False. Verse 40 says, “Now if a man loses his hair and is bald, he is still clean.” Verse 41 says a receding hairline is the same. The trouble comes only if there's a reddish-white sore on the bald head or forehead (Leviticus 13:42).

The answer is their mouth. Verse 45 says the person “…must cover his mouth and cry out, ‘Unclean, unclean!’” I think this is one of the heavy parts of the chapter. It's a hard way to live, and it's good to read it plainly.

The answer is alone outside the camp. Verse 46 says, “As long as he has the infection, he remains unclean. He must live alone in a place outside the camp.” That is the place the text gives for a person who has the infection. I think this one hurts to read.

The answer is green and red. Verse 49 says, “…if the mark in the fabric, leather, weave, knit, or leather article is green or red, then it is contaminated with mildew and must be shown to the priest.” So a green mark means a trip to the priest, and so does a red one. Green and red together are the pair. Neither one gets a pass.
The answer is to isolate it for seven days. Verse 50 says, “…the priest is to examine the mildew and isolate the contaminated fabric for seven days.” The item gets its own seven-day wait.
The answer is that it is burned up. Verse 52 says, “Since the mildew is harmful, the article must be burned up.” That covers wool, linen or leather. Once the mildew has spread, the item is done.

The answer is False. Verse 55 says, “Even though the mildew has not spread, you must burn it, whether the rot is on the front or back.” The washing didn't change how it looks, so the item is unclean. Not spreading isn't enough here.

The answer is burn the item, friends! Verse 57 says, “But if it reappears in the fabric, weave, or knit, or on any leather article, it is spreading. You must burn the contaminated article.” The priest already tried cutting out the mildewed section in verse 56. When the mildew comes back, the text doesn't send him for a second snip. It says burn.

The answer is True. Verse 58 says, “If the mildew disappears from the fabric, weave, or knit, or any leather article after washing, then it is to be washed again, and it will be clean.” One more wash and the item is clean. A happy ending for a piece of laundry.
